physicians.name: Dr. Ruth Ellery
physicians.shortBio: Sees general dermatology four days a week and runs the practice's surgical list on Thursdays. Particular interest in skin cancer of the head and neck.

physicians.name: Dr. Alan Fenwick
physicians.shortBio: Splits his week between the Portland office and the Brunswick satellite. Takes most of the practice's paediatric referrals.

services.name: Full skin examination
services.shortDescription: A head-to-toe check, usually annually, and the appointment most people should book first.

services.name: Acne
services.shortDescription: From first-line topicals through to isotretinoin, managed in the office.

services.name: Eczema and psoriasis
services.shortDescription: Including biologic therapy where it is warranted.

services.name: Skin cancer surgery
services.shortDescription: Excision and repair, on site, with pathology read locally.

services.name: Teledermatology review
services.shortDescription: For established patients with a new spot who would otherwise wait weeks.

services.name: Second opinion on a biopsy result

brand.tone: Medical first, unhurried, plainly written. A practice that would rather be trusted than admired.
brand.photography: Available light, the real rooms and the real coast. No models, no stock.

proof.claim: Both physicians are certified by the American Board of Dermatology.

concept.thesis: The appointment most people need is the one they cannot find on your website.
concept.positioning: A medical dermatology practice whose surgical work is its quiet strength, currently presented as a list of services with no order of importance.
knownProblems: The full skin examination — the reason most new patients call — is fourteenth in an alphabetical list of services.
The two physicians appear as names and credentials with no photograph and no sense of what each of them actually does.
On a phone the address and the telephone number are three taps from the home page.
The surgical work, which is the practice's real depth, is one line under "Procedures".
proposedImprovements: Lead with the examination and let everything else sit beneath it.
Give each physician a page written like a person rather than a directory row.
Put the telephone number and the address in reach from every screen.
Group services the way a patient thinks about them — medical, surgical, access — not alphabetically.
outOfScope: Booking is a link to whatever system the practice already runs; nothing here replaces a scheduler.
Photography is indicated, not supplied — the plates are placeholders until a shoot happens.
No patient-facing forms, and nothing that could receive health information.

findings.text: The practice lists two physicians and a Brunswick satellite location.
The site's services page lists 24 items in a single alphabetical column.
On a 390px screen the header pushes the first real content below two folds.
The telephone number appears only in the footer and is not a tel: link.
Most inbound calls are for a general skin check rather than for a named procedure — worth confirming with the front desk before the concept commits to that hierarchy.
Proposed hero line: “Start with the full skin examination. Everything else follows from what it finds.”
